basis: Independent source review and every current skill/step, including setup, teaching, criterion, easier option, dependencies and claim scope. Exact sequences are editorial adaptations, not clinically validated protocols.

historicalReasons.LEAVE-2: A protected floor item can be taught behind a barrier; wearing a harness is a setup option, not a learning component.
historicalReasons.LAUNDRY-1: A close cloth deposit needs basket release, not a completed outward retrieve.
historicalReasons.LAUNDRY-2: The floor cloth pickup explicitly requires FETCH-2 when it is introduced.
historicalReasons.SHELF-1: Introducing the carrier at the hand needs give; floor/shelf pickup follows separately.
historicalReasons.SHELF-2: Mock-shelf pickup and delivery explicitly require FETCH-2.
historicalReasons.FREE-1: Any comfortable position supports release; a finished sit was an artificial gate.
historicalReasons.BOX-1: A basket release needs give, not an outward retrieve.
historicalReasons.BOX-2: Floor pickup and carry still need FETCH-2 as well as the basket deposit.
historicalReasons.CLOSE-1: Door-pad work builds on the independent object target instead of hand targeting.
historicalReasons.OPEN-1: Appliance movement comfort can be learned before rope pulling.
historicalReasons.OPEN-2: Actual door pulling explicitly requires PULL-3 and appliance comfort.
historicalReasons.SHELF-3: Fridge retrieval needs appliance comfort as well as mock-shelf retrieval.
historicalReasons.CLOSE-3: Transfer to this appliance also requires comfortable appliance movement.
historicalReasons.DRINK-1: Rehearse the retrieval ending independently; opening is needed when added at DRINK-2.
historicalReasons.DRINK-2: Joining opening and pickup requires OPEN-3; PULL-3 is directly visible here as well.
historicalReasons.TURN-2: The learned turn is necessary; suitable comfortable equipment is a direct setup check rather than a mandatory harness grade.
historicalReasons.TEETH-1: Brush appearance is independent of a chin rest.
historicalReasons.TEETH-2: Lip touch uses the voluntary start/exit signal established by CHIN-2.
historicalReasons.WEAVE-2: The other loop can be taught from the same MIDDLE foundation without learning the first loop.
historicalReasons.WEAVE-3: The joined figure eight requires both independent loops.
historicalReasons.CARDS-1: The first symbol uses an already familiar pose; hand targeting belongs at the second symbol.
historicalReasons.TOYNAME-1: Enjoyable toy-label pairing does not require a retrieve.
historicalReasons.TWOOBJECT-1: The second toy label can be taught separately; its criterion now concerns that pair alone.
historicalReasons.TWOOBJECT-2: Mixed choices require both the first toy association and the independently taught second one.
historicalReasons.CARDS-2: The second symbol can be paired with the known touch independently of the first symbol.
historicalReasons.CARDS-3: Mixed symbol choices require both symbol-action pairings.
historicalReasons.POUCH-1: An empty pouch handover needs give; carrying is introduced at the next step.
historicalReasons.POUCH-2: Moving with the pouch requires CARRY-1 alongside its familiar handover.
historicalReasons.MESSENGER-1: Giving to the second person can be taught before the carry.
historicalReasons.MESSENGER-2: Moving toward that person requires CARRY-1 as well as the handover.
historicalReasons.RECALL-1: A distinct recall cue can be paired directly with approach; responding to the dog’s name is independent.
historicalReasons.RESTHEAD-1: This step teaches cushion contact directly; a hand chin rest is only an optional prompt.
historicalReasons.SETTLE-1: Voluntary rest on a comfortable mat can be captured without a trained go-to-mat cue.
historicalReasons.LOOSE-1: Comfortable secure equipment is checked directly; recording a harness lesson is not a necessary learned component.
historicalReasons.RECALLCTX-1: The indoor recall transfers; comfortable fitted long-line equipment is a safety condition, not an extra obedience prerequisite.
historicalReasons.STORM-1: Support and management must be accessible immediately; this step rehearses the refuge itself without requiring an earlier grade.
historicalReasons.BOXFIND-1: An obvious reward in one open box teaches its own search; another food-search lesson adds no necessary component.
historicalReasons.WALKCTX-1: Transfer uses loose walking; a turn-away remains a useful optional exit, not part of the taught walking action.
historicalReasons.MATCTX-1: Moving the mat cue to a new room precedes resting and need not wait for settled duration.
historicalReasons.MATCTX-2: The quiet-rest component is required at the step that actually transfers it.
historicalReasons.SLIPPERS-1: Hand presentation uses take and give; the floor retrieve belongs at the floor step.
historicalReasons.SLIPPERS-2: Floor pickup and delivery now explicitly require the reusable retrieve at the point of use.
historicalReasons.HOOP-1: Exploring an opening and following a small optional lure can be taught directly; a finished hand target unnecessarily blocks exploration.
historicalReasons.WAVE-1: A small offered paw lift is sufficient; turning the palm into a high five is an optional detour.
historicalReasons.NAIL-2: Tool sight and sound can be conditioned separately from paw touch; this step stops before contact or clipping.
historicalReasons.FETCH-1: A stationary pickup from a lower surface uses known take/hold/give, covered by hand delivery; traveling carries are not used until the next step.
historicalReasons.FETCH-2: The short outward retrieve now explicitly requires carrying at the step that introduces travel.
historicalReasons.PASS-1: The first pass uses a stationary comfortable helper and a rehearsed exit; completed parallel moving-dog walks and sniff interruptions are unnecessary gates.
historicalReasons.PASS-2: The moving-helper pass now explicitly needs comfortable dog movement at the step that introduces it.
historicalReasons.ALONE-3: Departure actions can be conditioned independently; they must not be gated behind out-of-view absences or treated as proof of absence tolerance.
historicalReasons.CROSS-1: Indoor route rehearsal needs the flat-line pause, not completed exposure at a real curb.
historicalReasons.CROSS-2: Real crossing adds the actual curb context only when that context is introduced.
historicalReasons.VISITOR-4: An optional view must not become a gate for nonvisual visitor practice.
historicalReasons.OBJECT-3: Sound conditioning can begin independently of visible movement; combinations require both components to be comfortable.
historicalReasons.TRACKPERSON-2: Offering a sample does not teach its meaning. Route following can use visual, ground-disturbance or airborne cues.
historicalReasons.SCENTREPORT-1: Visible find-and-indicate chaining needs the visible article approach; partly concealed searching is not yet used.
historicalReasons.SCENTREPORT-3: The partly concealed search component becomes necessary only when this step introduces partial concealment.

NAME.rationale: Attention to a name is taught before distraction; a name is not assumed to be a recall or evidence of emotional comfort.

NAME-1.reason: Name-reward pairing precedes the offered head turn; neither requires a sit or eye contact.

NAME-2.reason: Name-reward pairing precedes the offered head turn; neither requires a sit or eye contact.

MARK.rationale: Pair the chosen gentle signal with prompt reward; markers are optional and no later action is required after a terminal marker.

MARK-1.reason: A marker can be paired directly with reward and must not become a universal training gate.

TOUCH.rationale: Voluntary empty-hand nose targeting transfers only after the basic contact; do not push a hand into the face.

TOUCH-1.reason: Voluntary palm contact precedes naming and small placement changes.

TOUCH-2.reason: Voluntary palm contact precedes naming and small placement changes.

SIT.rationale: Comfortable voluntary sitting and early lure fading are appropriate; sitting is not mandatory for safety or proof of calm.

SIT-1.reason: Comfortable sit acquisition precedes fading food and adding the cue; down and stand are independent.

SIT-2.reason: Comfortable sit acquisition precedes fading food and adding the cue; down and stand are independent.

DOWN.rationale: Reward comfortable voluntary lowering without restraint; posture is distinct from relaxation.

DOWN-1.reason: Unforced down acquisition precedes cue transfer; a completed sit is unnecessary.

DOWN-2.reason: Unforced down acquisition precedes cue transfer; a completed sit is unnecessary.

STAND.rationale: A comfortable stationary stand is useful independently of a down; avoid repeatedly luring the dog to walk forward.

STAND-1.reason: The dog may already offer a comfortable sit or rise naturally; a recorded sit grade is unnecessary.

FREE.rationale: A release can be taught from any comfortable position; a completed sit is an unnecessary prerequisite.

FREE-1.reason: Release can be paired from any offered comfortable position, then separated from in-position rewards.

FREE-2.reason: Release can be paired from any offered comfortable position, then separated from in-position rewards.

DROP.rationale: Trade willingly without chasing or prying; prevention and guarding assessment are distinct from a generic exchange exercise.

DROP-1.reason: Easy voluntary trades precede cue-before-reward release, with no retrieve requirement.

DROP-2.reason: Easy voluntary trades precede cue-before-reward release, with no retrieve requirement.

LEAVE.rationale: Retain the cue, separately reinforce offered disengagement, teach modest context transfer, and keep hazards inaccessible without supervision.

LEAVE-1.reason: Keep the first offered disengagement easy; prevent frustration and avoid implying that staring must continue until a cue.

LEAVE-2.reason: A cue can be useful without claiming unsupervised protection. The old title contradicted the protected setup.

LEAVE-3.reason: New context transfer needs its own record; it is not implied by learning the spoken cue.

LEAVE-4.reason: Handler-distance transfer is new learning. No absent-handler or household-wide safety claim is made.

WAIT.rationale: A short safe interior-door pause can be offered or cued; release and physical exit security remain explicit.

WAIT-1.reason: Offered doorway pauses are compatible with a release cue; reinforcement can include access through a safe interior doorway.

WAIT-2.reason: Door movement, waiting time and context are separate difficulty dimensions.

TOILET.rationale: Supervision, frequent individual opportunities and rewarding location are appropriate; medical changes are not disobedience.

TOILET-1.reason: Access routines precede cue pairing. Toilet access must never depend on obedience.

TOILET-2.reason: Access routines precede cue pairing. Toilet access must never depend on obedience.

RECALL.rationale: Teach a distinct inviting approach directly, then transfer gradually; do not assume reliability around hazards or punish arrival.

RECALL-1.reason: A distinct recall cue can be paired directly with approach; responding to the dog’s name is independent.

RECALL-2.reason: Recall words directly predict approach; a name response is helpful but not required.

OTARGET.rationale: Teach broad stationary nose contact before placement or motion; this is a reusable contact action, not emotional treatment.

OTARGET-1.reason: Direct nose contact is acquired before the object-target cue and placement changes.

OTARGET-2.reason: Direct nose contact is acquired before the object-target cue and placement changes.

STAY.rationale: Increase short duration, distance and distraction separately; release and comfort matter more than a posture quota.

STAY-1.reason: The release is an actual end signal; short duration precedes movement and small independent changes.

STAY-2.reason: The release is an actual end signal; short duration precedes movement and small independent changes.

STAY-3.reason: The release is an actual end signal; short duration precedes movement and small independent changes.

STOP.rationale: Reward a modest stationary pause in protected settings; this does not authorize traffic or off-leash safety tests.

STOP-1.reason: A familiar stand supports stopping slow movement, then reduced handler prompting and a tiny distance change.

STOP-2.reason: A familiar stand supports stopping slow movement, then reduced handler prompting and a tiny distance change.

STOP-3.reason: A familiar stand supports stopping slow movement, then reduced handler prompting and a tiny distance change.

FRONT.rationale: A comfortable arrival position is optional and distinct from a safety recall; do not crowd or physically align the dog.

FRONT-1.reason: A broad comfortable approach directly teaches the front position; no completed recall or sit is necessary.

FRONT-2.reason: A broad comfortable approach directly teaches the front position; no completed recall or sit is necessary.

FOODWAIT.rationale: Keep bowl placement very brief and optional; never make meals conditional, repeatedly remove bowls, or treat guarding through compliance.

FOODWAIT-1.reason: Bowl manners are optional; essential nutrition and guarding treatment must not depend on compliance.

FOODWAIT-2.reason: A momentary pause is paired directly with bowl access; meals and urgent access never depend on a grade.

MAT.rationale: Teach voluntary stationing and release separately from relaxed rest; a mat is not an enforced place to endure fear.

MAT-1.reason: Approach and full-foot arrival precede adding the mat cue; settling and staying are separate behaviors.

MAT-2.reason: Approach and full-foot arrival precede adding the mat cue; settling and staying are separate behaviors.

SETTLE.rationale: Capture comfortable rest independently of cued stationing; a down, food-taking or immobility alone does not establish relaxation.

SETTLE-1.reason: Voluntary rest on a comfortable mat can be captured without a trained go-to-mat cue.

SETTLE-2.reason: Voluntary rest is captured directly; go-to-mat is an optional aid rather than a gate.

SETTLE-3.reason: Voluntary rest is captured directly; go-to-mat is an optional aid rather than a gate.

SAFE.rationale: A refuge requires actual comfort, escape management and trusted support; confinement or isolation is not automatically soothing.

SAFE-1.reason: Refuge exploration precedes attended management rehearsals. There is no requirement to be left alone.

SAFE-2.reason: Refuge exploration precedes attended management rehearsals. There is no requirement to be left alone.

ALONE.rationale: Camera-guided below-distress movement, tiny absences and departure-action comfort are distinct components; no crying-out or duration guarantee.

ALONE-1.reason: Comfortable tiny within-room movements precede tiny absences and departure-action combinations.

ALONE-2.reason: Comfortable tiny within-room movements precede tiny absences and departure-action combinations.

ALONE-3.reason: Departure actions can be conditioned independently; they must not be gated behind out-of-view absences or treated as proof of absence tolerance.

RESTHEAD.rationale: Voluntary cushion contact can be taught directly; do not press the head down or infer calm solely from the trained posture.

RESTHEAD-1.reason: This step teaches cushion contact directly; a hand chin rest is only an optional prompt.

RESTHEAD-2.reason: Cushion contact is shaped directly; a hand chin rest is an optional prompt rather than a prerequisite.

CRATE.rationale: Introduce an optional crate with voluntary entry and gradual comfortable closure; it is unsuitable as compulsory panic management.

CRATE-1.reason: Voluntary entry precedes door motion, then tiny attended closure. Open refuge, absences and travel remain distinct.

CRATE-2.reason: Voluntary entry precedes door motion, then tiny attended closure. Open refuge, absences and travel remain distinct.

CRATE-3.reason: Voluntary entry precedes door motion, then tiny attended closure. Open refuge, absences and travel remain distinct.

VACATE.rationale: Reward moving to an inviting alternative without crowding, intimidation or grabbing; existing guarding requires an individual plan.

VACATE-1.reason: A voluntary route to a safe low landing precedes cue transfer; no pressure or high jump.

VACATE-2.reason: A voluntary route to a safe low landing precedes cue transfer; no pressure or high jump.

ALLDONE.rationale: Pair a predictable end signal with a comfortable transition; it is not punishment or enforced loss of needed interaction.

ALLDONE-1.reason: A predictable pleasant transition acquires the end cue directly before transfer to another activity.

ALLDONE-2.reason: A predictable pleasant transition acquires the end cue directly before transfer to another activity.

CHECK.rationale: Reinforce offered check-ins and gradual transfer; do not demand prolonged eye contact or make food pairing contingent on it.

CHECK-1.reason: Offered orientation is rewarded directly before incorporating ordinary walking.

CHECK-2.reason: Offered orientation is rewarded directly before incorporating ordinary walking.

LOOSE.rationale: Teach slack-lead walking on comfortable equipment in small increments; equipment fit is a safety check rather than an obedience grade.

LOOSE-1.reason: Comfortable secure equipment is checked directly; recording a harness lesson is not a necessary learned component.

LOOSE-2.reason: Slack-leash movement is taught directly; secure comfortable equipment is checked in the setup, without requiring a harness grade.

LOOSE-3.reason: Slack-leash movement is taught directly; secure comfortable equipment is checked in the setup, without requiring a harness grade.

TURN.rationale: Rehearse an inviting turn before mild distraction, without leash corrections; a retreat remains valid regardless of cue response.

TURN-1.reason: A trigger-free turn cue precedes travel and easy sniff interruptions; equipment comfort is a setup condition.

TURN-2.reason: The learned turn is necessary; suitable comfortable equipment is a direct setup check rather than a mandatory harness grade.

TURN-3.reason: A trigger-free turn cue precedes travel and easy sniff interruptions; equipment comfort is a setup condition.

FIND.rationale: Invited food search on known safe ground is compatible with leave-it training; avoid competition, ingestion hazards or overwhelming triggers.

FIND-1.reason: A visible food scatter acquires its own cue before the ground surface changes.

FIND-2.reason: A visible food scatter acquires its own cue before the ground surface changes.

SIDE.rationale: Reward a comfortable side position without physical placement; this optional alignment does not replace free movement and sniffing.

SIDE-1.reason: The hand target actually guides the broad route; the far-side cue follows this action.

SIDE-2.reason: The hand target actually guides the broad route; the far-side cue follows this action.

HEEL.rationale: Short precise positioning is optional, with early lure fading and releases; it is not the standard for an entire ordinary walk.

HEEL-1.reason: Entry position is independently trainable; brief movement precedes turns and a learned release at the step that uses its discrimination.

HEEL-2.reason: Entry position is independently trainable; brief movement precedes turns and a learned release at the step that uses its discrimination.

HEEL-3.reason: Entry position is independently trainable; brief movement precedes turns and a learned release at the step that uses its discrimination.

HEEL-4.reason: Entry position is independently trainable; brief movement precedes turns and a learned release at the step that uses its discrimination.

RHYTHM.rationale: Predictable short walking patterns can help communication; no claim that a pattern cures fear or overrides the need for distance.

RHYTHM-1.reason: Predictable stationary count-reward pairings precede a few optional walking cycles; exact heel position and trigger exposure are not part of this game.

RHYTHM-2.reason: Predictable stationary count-reward pairings precede a few optional walking cycles; exact heel position and trigger exposure are not part of this game.

CURB.rationale: Start at harmless flat lines, then a protected real curb with human traffic decisions; no automatic road-safety claim.

CURB-1.reason: A harmless floor line teaches the pause before quiet real-edge transfer; no claim that dogs judge traffic.

CURB-2.reason: A harmless floor line teaches the pause before quiet real-edge transfer; no claim that dogs judge traffic.

CROSS.rationale: Indoor rehearsal follows flat-line preparation; the actual curb prerequisite moves to the real crossing, where humans decide safety.

CROSS-1.reason: Indoor route rehearsal needs the flat-line pause, not completed exposure at a real curb.

CROSS-2.reason: Real crossing adds the actual curb context only when that context is introduced.

SLOW.rationale: Reward modest changes to walking pace without force; exercise and pace must suit individual health and normal movement.

SLOW-1.reason: Known slack-leash steps support a small pace change, then a few slower steps.

SLOW-2.reason: Known slack-leash steps support a small pace change, then a few slower steps.

WALKPAUSE.rationale: Practice brief comfortable pauses and release rather than prolonged suppression of exploration or distress.

WALKPAUSE-1.reason: A direct short pause beside a stopped human precedes a brief ordinary hand movement; formal heel is unnecessary.

WALKPAUSE-2.reason: A direct short pause beside a stopped human precedes a brief ordinary hand movement; formal heel is unnecessary.

DOG.rationale: Brief supported sightings and prompt trigger-food pairing begin at a comfortable distance; no obedience or threshold testing is required.

DOG-1.reason: Assessment should not withhold support until a later lesson.

DOG-2.reason: An individually comfortable sighting precedes positive pairings, then small controlled movement changes.

DOG-3.reason: An individually comfortable sighting precedes positive pairings, then small controlled movement changes.

DISENGAGE.rationale: Teach an offered attention shift at an easy distance, distinct from counterconditioning; never wait through escalating fixation.

DISENGAGE-1.reason: Easy sight-food pairing supports comfortable observation before rewarding offered look-aways; no required stare or obedience pose.

DISENGAGE-2.reason: Easy sight-food pairing supports comfortable observation before rewarding offered look-aways; no required stare or obedience pose.

PARALLEL.rationale: Both dogs need comfortable wide movement and retreat; trigger-food support need not wait for a check-in or eventual greeting.

PARALLEL-1.reason: Maintain trigger-food pairing during comfortable movement; check-ins are separately reinforced rather than a condition of support.

PARALLEL-2.reason: Comfort with a moving helper dog and a rehearsed turn support controlled walking and safe exits.

PASS.rationale: The first stationary-helper pass needs dog comfort and a turn; moving-helper competence is introduced only for a moving pass.

PASS-1.reason: The first pass uses a stationary comfortable helper and a rehearsed exit; completed parallel moving-dog walks and sniff interruptions are unnecessary gates.

PASS-2.reason: The moving-helper pass now explicitly needs comfortable dog movement at the step that introduces it.

STRANGER.rationale: Use a distant neutral adult with optional retreat, no food lure toward touch and no obligatory greeting.

STRANGER-1.reason: Comfortable stationary distant sightings precede tiny adult movements and separate generalization to another person.

STRANGER-2.reason: Comfortable stationary distant sightings precede tiny adult movements and separate generalization to another person.

STRANGER-3.reason: Comfortable stationary distant sightings precede tiny adult movements and separate generalization to another person.

KNOCK.rationale: Separate a faint controllable tap from mat behavior and the real arrival chain; do not repeat overwhelming knocks waiting for quiet.

KNOCK-1.reason: A faint harmless tap precedes transfer to the entryway and small changes of count or intensity.

KNOCK-2.reason: A faint harmless tap precedes transfer to the entryway and small changes of count or intensity.

KNOCK-3.reason: A faint harmless tap precedes transfer to the entryway and small changes of count or intensity.

BELL.rationale: Faint recording and physical bell are separate contexts; pair the noticed sound without requiring silence or a station first.

BELL-1.reason: A faint recording precedes a controllable real bell. An unmodifiable frightening bell needs management, not forced advancement.

BELL-2.reason: A faint recording precedes a controllable real bell. An unmodifiable frightening bell needs management, not forced advancement.

DOOR.rationale: Combine fluent arrival components under controlled rehearsal; an entry-management plan remains necessary for unplanned arrivals.

DOOR-1.reason: The comfortable practical knock, mat arrival and release are actual links in this cue chain; handler door movement follows it.

DOOR-2.reason: The comfortable practical knock, mat arrival and release are actual links in this cue chain; handler door movement follows it.

DOOR-3.reason: The comfortable practical knock, mat arrival and release are actual links in this cue chain; handler door movement follows it.

VISITOR.rationale: A fully separated comfortable visit is a valid endpoint; optional distant viewing must not block nonvisual visitor-action practice.

VISITOR-1.reason: Comfortable refuge management precedes actual arrivals; distant viewing explicitly uses the familiar stranger-comfort work.

VISITOR-2.reason: Comfortable refuge management precedes actual arrivals; distant viewing explicitly uses the familiar stranger-comfort work.

VISITOR-3.reason: Comfortable refuge management precedes actual arrivals; distant viewing explicitly uses the familiar stranger-comfort work.

VISITOR-4.reason: An optional view must not become a gate for nonvisual visitor practice.

GREET.rationale: Greeting is voluntary and unnecessary for successful coexistence; approach for food is not permission to touch.

GREET-1.reason: Four-paw comfort during an easy approach precedes optional voluntary contact; sitting is not required.

GREET-2.reason: Four-paw comfort during an easy approach precedes optional voluntary contact; sitting is not required.

HANDOFF.rationale: Use a familiar consenting helper and reversible small changes; transferred equipment does not justify restraint or separation distress.

HANDOFF-1.reason: Comfort with both familiar adults precedes a stationary controlled lead transfer and only then a few steps.

HANDOFF-2.reason: Comfort with both familiar adults precedes a stationary controlled lead transfer and only then a few steps.

HANDOFF-3.reason: Comfort with both familiar adults precedes a stationary controlled lead transfer and only then a few steps.

SOUND.rationale: Controlled brief sound-food pairing changes one dimension at a time; replace historical no-comfort guidance and avoid recording-to-real-event guarantees.

SOUND-1.reason: One comfortable low-intensity pairing precedes one-variable changes and source transfer.

SOUND-2.reason: One comfortable low-intensity pairing precedes one-variable changes and source transfer.

SOUND-3.reason: One comfortable low-intensity pairing precedes one-variable changes and source transfer.

OUTSIDE.rationale: Different mild outdoor sights and sounds need separately controlled starts; visual and auditory presentations are not interchangeable certification.

OUTSIDE-1.reason: Management and easy event pairings precede adding the already learned turn away at the action that uses it.

OUTSIDE-2.reason: Management and easy event pairings precede adding the already learned turn away at the action that uses it.

OUTSIDE-3.reason: Management and easy event pairings precede adding the already learned turn away at the action that uses it.

STORM.rationale: Rehearse protection and support before real events; plan readiness can be recorded without inducing noise or claiming fear is cured.

STORM-1.reason: Support and management must be accessible immediately; this step rehearses the refuge itself without requiring an earlier grade.

STORM-2.reason: A support plan can be ready before an unavoidable event occurs. Completion must not require manufactured exposure or imply a cure.

OBJECT.rationale: Still sight, motion and sound can be conditioned separately; food does not require exploration, and combinations await comfortable components.

OBJECT-1.reason: Counterconditioning does not require approach, calm exploration or obedience before food.

OBJECT-2.reason: Comfortable sight precedes small object movement, then separately introduced appliance sound.

OBJECT-3.reason: Sound conditioning can begin independently of visible movement; combinations require both components to be comfortable.

MOTION.rationale: Start well away from traffic or controlled moving helpers with retreat; use physical security and avoid motion-based flooding.

MOTION-1.reason: Comfortable distant slow movement precedes a tiny speed or duration change; no approach or chase.

MOTION-2.reason: Comfortable distant slow movement precedes a tiny speed or duration change; no approach or chase.

CAR.rationale: Stationary-car comfort precedes travel; use appropriate transport restraint and veterinary assessment of motion sickness or severe distress.

CAR-1.reason: Comfortable observation precedes voluntary entry, then stationary restraint and door-closure preparation.

CAR-2.reason: Comfortable observation precedes voluntary entry, then stationary restraint and door-closure preparation.

CAR-3.reason: Comfortable observation precedes voluntary entry, then stationary restraint and door-closure preparation.

ELEVATOR.rationale: Introduce empty-car sounds, voluntary entry and a short ride separately; keep dog and handler together with no leash through closing doors.

ELEVATOR-1.reason: Door-cycle observation precedes stationary voluntary entry before a tiny attended ride.

ELEVATOR-2.reason: Prevent a line crossing a closing elevator door; enter and exit together with ordinary short equipment.

ELEVATOR-3.reason: Door-cycle observation precedes stationary voluntary entry before a tiny attended ride.

AUTODOOR.rationale: Observe safely before a controlled broad passage; never rely on a sensor detecting a dog or put the dog in the opening to activate it.

AUTODOOR-1.reason: Comfortable panel observation precedes a fully human-checked wide passage; a trained hoop pass is unrelated.

AUTODOOR-2.reason: Keep handler and dog together, and ordinary leash clear of automatic doors.

HARNESS.rationale: Voluntary approach, head passage and comfortable fitting are separate; fit, movement and withdrawal matter more than a completed grade.

HARNESS-1.reason: Appearance and buckle comfort precede voluntary placement, then fastening and a few steps.

HARNESS-2.reason: Appearance and buckle comfort precede voluntary placement, then fastening and a few steps.

HARNESS-3.reason: Appearance and buckle comfort precede voluntary placement, then fastening and a few steps.

MUZZLE.rationale: Use a properly fitted basket allowing full panting and drinking, voluntary entry and gradual straps; no unattended wear or exposure beyond comfort.

MUZZLE-1.reason: Appearance precedes voluntary entry, tiny duration, straps, then comfortable movement; none certifies exposure safety.

MUZZLE-2.reason: Appearance precedes voluntary entry, tiny duration, straps, then comfortable movement; none certifies exposure safety.

MUZZLE-3.reason: Appearance precedes voluntary entry, tiny duration, straps, then comfortable movement; none certifies exposure safety.

MUZZLE-4.reason: Appearance precedes voluntary entry, tiny duration, straps, then comfortable movement; none certifies exposure safety.

MUZZLE-5.reason: Appearance precedes voluntary entry, tiny duration, straps, then comfortable movement; none certifies exposure safety.

CHIN.rationale: A voluntary start and immediate withdrawal are trained communication, not proof of calm or permission to hold the dog through discomfort.

CHIN-1.reason: Direct voluntary contact precedes a short freely ended start signal.

CHIN-2.reason: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

HANDLE.rationale: Healthy shoulder movement and momentary touch precede small changes; stop for whole-body discomfort even if the chin remains in position.

HANDLE-1.reason: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

HANDLE-2.reason: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

BRUSH.rationale: Separate tool presence, tiny strokes and small area/duration changes; mats, pain and forced grooming need an individual professional plan.

BRUSH-1.reason: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

BRUSH-2.reason: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

NAIL.rationale: Paw handling and tool presence can be learned separately; no app completion authorizes clipping anatomy or restraining a paw.

NAIL-1.reason: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

NAIL-2.reason: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

TEETH.rationale: Use veterinary demonstration, pain assessment and pet-safe materials; tiny voluntary lip and outer-tooth work do not replace dental care.

TEETH-1.reason: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

TEETH-2.reason: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

TEETH-3.reason: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

SCALE.rationale: Secure low non-slip surfaces and voluntary steps precede a reading pause; avoid lifting paws or slippery elevated equipment.

SCALE-1.reason: Surface comfort precedes voluntary entry, then a short supported weigh-in pause.

SCALE-2.reason: Surface comfort precedes voluntary entry, then a short supported weigh-in pause.

SCALE-3.reason: Surface comfort precedes voluntary entry, then a short supported weigh-in pause.

CLIP.rationale: Tiny sound and approach precede clip contact; equipment operation and whole-body comfort remain separate checks.

CLIP-1.reason: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.

CLIP-2.reason: Voluntary participation includes whole-body comfort and a real stop, not only maintaining a trained posture.
